name: tool-result-file-source-passes-through
description: a TOOL_CALL_RESULT whose content carries a part sourced from a provider-held file mints a tool message holding that source unchanged — type, handle, provider and mimeType — with no warning; the handle is opaque, so a client may neither rewrite it as a URL nor drop the part for carrying a source arm it does not itself resolve
kill: make the client's strip stage treat an unknown-looking source arm as unrecognised material and drop the part, or have the TOOL_CALL_RESULT reducer rewrite a file source as a url source

dotnet.intentional: the .NET client assembles history through Microsoft.Extensions.AI ChatMessages, and a FunctionResultContent holds one result object: the tool result's parts are flattened to their text (AGUIContent.ToString) and the tool message takes the tool call's id, so the file-sourced document part does not survive into the assembled messages. The event itself carries the part — AGUIToolMessage and ToolCallResultEvent hold AGUIContent, whose source union includes the file arm — and a parts-preserving mapping onto MEAI content is tracked separately. The flattening is lossy, and the specification asks a consumer to announce a lossy rendering rather than let a dropped part look like one the producer never sent, so .NET warns once for the result — which is why `noWarnings` cannot hold on this lane and is replaced by the warning it does emit. TypeScript keeps the parts and so has nothing to announce.
